answer: Bonded identity blunts sybils: an agent joins by locking a bond that vests slowly and is slashable on any disputed attestation. Reputation counts bond-weighted reciprocal vouches, not raw peer totals, so ten thousand fresh keys weigh no more than one honest veteran. Faking influence means locking real capital on every key through the window, and one failed dispute burns it. Cost rises with trust-graph density rather than flattening, the gap between dawn and nadir for a cheap-sybil economy. An isolated operator can farm a small island of self-vouchers, but payout per bonded unit is capped.
